lesson.title: Estimate, then measure
lesson.subtitle: P4 angle revision
lesson.objective: Estimate an angle by comparing it with 90 degrees, then measure it.
lesson.story: An angle is drawn on a protractor.

steps.title: Estimate first
steps.prompt: Before you measure, which is the best estimate for this angle?
hints: Compare the angle with a right angle, 90 degrees, and with half a right angle, 45 degrees.
Is the angle smaller or larger than a right angle?
The angle is larger than a right angle, so some estimates are far too small.

steps.title: Now measure it
steps.prompt: Now measure the angle with the protractor. What is its size in degrees?
hints: Read where the second arm crosses the scale that starts at 0 on the base arm.
Long marks are every 10 degrees and short marks are every 5 degrees. Count along from 0.
The arm crosses just after 160, exactly on that long mark.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why is it helpful to estimate before you measure?

choices.label: It tells you the exact size, so the protractor reading must match it exactly.
It helps you spot a reading that is far off, like one from the wrong scale.
A good estimate is close enough, so you can skip measuring the angle at all.

hints: An estimate tells you roughly what to expect.
If your reading is very different, something went wrong.
Choose the explanation about noticing a reading that is far off.
